_meta.description: stdout decoding ground truth for scripts/test-stdout-decoding.js. Unlike hook-cleaning-ground-truth.json (which measures text CLEANING), this measures DECODING IDENTITY: encode a known line to a known byte encoding, feed the raw bytes to TextractorLauncher._processStdoutData() split at various chunk boundaries, and the lines the launcher emits via its 'output' event must equal the originals EXACTLY, byte for byte in the resulting string. Any deviation is a decoder bug, not a text-cleaning judgment call.
_meta.whyOutputEvent: Assertions read the 'output' event because it fires after _sanitizeLine().trim() and before _parseHookLine/_cleanGameText/text-cleaning.js — the right altitude for a pure decoding bench: it is insensitive to the cleaning/dedup logic this change deliberately does not touch (see plan Fase 2.5, 'Que NO tocar'). Reference lines therefore must not have leading/trailing whitespace, must be >= 2 chars (the launcher's own minimum), and must not trip _isOwnEcho (no literal '[Textractor]'/'[Tuhua]'/'[Pipeline]', no 'Usage:' + 'attach'/'hookcode', no bare '$ ' prefix, no 'A:\...' drive-letter prompt pattern).
_meta.confirmedBug: Root cause reproduced directly against this file's companion bench, in plain Node, before any fix was applied: a first stdout chunk of 1 or 3 raw bytes defeats the old `data.length >= 4` gate in _processStdoutData, so encoding detection is skipped for that chunk, it decodes as the 'utf8' default, and its trailing odd byte is DROPPED (the old carry-over logic only ran once encoding was already known to be utf16le). The next chunk then starts at an odd byte offset, which desyncs _isUtf16Le's own odd/even byte check and makes IT decide utf8 too — locking the entire session to the wrong encoding. _sanitizeLine then strips every decoded U+0000, so literal ASCII bytes survive perfectly intact while Japanese bytes decode to private-use-area garbage in the SAME string — exactly the reported symptom (ASCII 'Am' next to PUA U+E26B).

lines.note: Plain ASCII hook line, Format A header + English prose text.

止 U+6B62 + モ U+30E2 -> UTF-16LE bytes 62 6b e2 30. A 1-byte-shifted read of those four bytes decodes '6b e2' as U+E26B — the EXACT private-use-area character from the bug report — sitting next to literal ASCII 'Am' in the same string. This is the single most important row in the whole bench.

Hiragana + full-width punctuation. High byte 0x30 (hiragana range) is also ASCII '0' if UTF-16LE is misread as UTF-8 — the classic '0'-after-every-glyph corruption signature documented in the code's own v3.13.24 comment.

lines.text: [6:7394:74ECB850:ECB87D:0::HB0@0:nekopara_vol1_trial.exe] ネコパラ ヴォリューム
lines.note: Katakana, includes a dakuten-combined character (ヴ) and a long vowel mark (ー).

lines.text: [6:7394:74ECB850:ECB87D:0::HB0@0:nekopara_vol1_trial.exe] 恵麻さんは再び液タブへ視線を落とす。
lines.note: Real-shape Nekopara-style dialogue: kanji + hiragana + katakana + punctuation mixed, no ASCII at all after the header.
Non-BMP characters (surrogate pairs): 𠮷 U+20BB7 and the mathematical double-struck U U+1D54C. Exercises 4-byte UTF-16LE code units, which StringDecoder must keep intact across chunk boundaries.
Full-width Latin/digits/punctuation (U+FF00-FF60 range) — must not be confused with PUA by the plausibility scorer.
Format B system hook (Consola), all-ASCII, short. Also used as the S7_short_stream case to exercise the sub-minimum-sniff / flush-on-close path.

lines.text: そんなことないよ、ちゃんと見てるから
lines.note: H3: pure Japanese with NO ASCII header at all. _isUtf16Le(buf) returns FALSE on this in real UTF-16LE bytes (verified directly) because its high bytes are 0x30/0x4E-0x9F, never the 0x00 the heuristic's odd-byte check requires — the >0.5-nulls-in-odd-bytes / >0.5-printable-in-even-bytes heuristic is tuned for ASCII-heavy streams and is blind to CJK-heavy ones. The plausibility tiebreaker (scored against PUA/U+FFFD density) is what must catch this case instead.

Deliberately tiny: as UTF-16LE + trailing newline this is only 6 raw bytes total, well under the ~16-byte minimum sample the encoding sniffer needs before it will decide on its own. The only way this line is ever emitted is via the close/flush path deciding an encoding from a sub-minimum sample when the stream ends — covers the 'process dies before enough bytes accumulate' case from Fase 2.1.

streams.note: Baseline: ASCII-heavy first line lets _isUtf16Le's fast path decide immediately. Also carries the pua_trigger line — this must reconstruct EXACTLY under every split mode, including hostile.
Leading FF FE BOM should be authoritative and decide the encoding immediately, before any heuristic or plausibility scoring runs.
H3 direct repro: no BOM, no ASCII-heavy first chunk, pure Japanese. Must still land on utf16le via the plausibility tiebreaker, not fall back to utf8 (which would corrupt the entire stream).
Surrogate pairs and full-width forms must survive every chunk split, including a split that lands exactly between the two 16-bit code units of a surrogate pair.

Regression guard: a genuinely UTF-8-encoded stream (containing real CJK text, so it's not just ASCII-trivial) must NOT be dragged to utf16le by the new plausibility tiebreaker. The utf8-favoring margin exists specifically to protect this case.
EF BB BF UTF-8 BOM must be recognized and decide utf8 immediately.
Format B (system hook) header reconstructed exactly under fuzzing — a plain regression fixture, distinct from the sub-minimum-sniff case below.

Only 6 raw bytes total (see tiny_ack) — well under the encoding sniffer's minimum sample size. The line can only ever be emitted via the close/flush path deciding from a sub-minimum sample; a decoder that just drops incomplete sniff buffers on close fails this case with zero emitted lines.

Textractor never emits UTF-16BE — detecting it structurally (nulls in EVEN byte positions instead of odd, the mirror image of _isUtf16Le) means something upstream is wrong (corrupted pipe, wrong process). The assertion here is that an 'encoding-warning' event with encoding:'utf16be' fires, not that the text decodes correctly (Node has no built-in UTF-16BE decoder).
FE FF BOM (UTF-16BE) must also route through the same encoding-warning path, not be silently misdecoded as utf16le (FF FE) by a careless byte-order check.
